data.hypothesis: A 2048-element input tile may recover some parallelism lost by the selected 8192-element tile. For n=4,194,304 it emits 2048 int64 partials; reducing these in parallel groups of 128 produces 16 partials before finalization, adding a kernel versus the best visible two-kernel design. Keeping the 128-thread shared-memory reduction tree fixed tests whether that added partial stage pays for itself in full-call time.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use for T1 global-topology comparisons; these are whole-call results and do not establish which mechanism caused the differences.
memory_lessons.claim: The visible 4096-element-tile candidate measured 7.81568 µs across three samples, while the selected 8192-element-tile parent measured 17.44128 µs. The 128-element-tile candidates measured about 44.2 µs. These distinct valid outcomes motivate testing a contrasting tile and partial-stage topology, without assuming why one was faster.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this 2048-element input tile with 128-partial parallel stages against the two-kernel 4096-element candidate, using repeated full-call measurements.

data.notes: The visible 4096- and 8192-element-tile candidates were correct on all 10 reported cases and each had three timing samples; their means were 7.81568 µs and 17.44128 µs, respectively. The 128-element-tile candidates measured about 44.2 µs. This candidate keeps the 128-thread intra-block tree and uses 2048 input elements per CTA, then parallel 128-partial stages until at most 128 remain. At n=4,194,304 that means 2048 initial partials, then 16, then direct finalization: three kernels versus two for the visible 4096-tile design. No new variant has been measured here; the controller should validate and provide repeated full-call measurements. No failed variant is reported in the supplied observations.
transformations: Kept the 128-thread shared-memory intra-block reduction tree and int64 intermediate sums.
Changed the bounded input tile to 2048 elements and assigned intermediate partial reductions to 128-element tiles, yielding a parallel stage before finalization for large partial counts.
Recursively reduces partials until at most 128 remain, then writes the exact total directly to out; uses two packed scratch buffers without reading uninitialized entries.
Retained the bounded direct path, zero handling, required-pointer checks, and default-stream kernel launches.
